predictions.title: Reservoir routing ships as default vLLM and SGLang serving knob by H2 2026
predictions.body: By H2 2026 the Reservoir Routing stateful Mixture-of-Experts primitive â€” first published Wednesday on arxiv.org/abs/2605.10142 by Stanford CRFM PhD candidate Aryaman Arora and DeepMind senior research scientist Aakanksha Chowdhery â€” lands as a default-tunable serving-stack knob in both vLLM and SGLang on frontier-class MoE backbones, with the router-state-bank caching expert-selection trajectories across multi-turn agentic conversations rather than recomputing routing at every token. The paper reports a 4.1 percentage-point SWE-Bench Verified uplift on the 145B MoE backbone (Qwen3 MoE 60B uplifted with the Tsinghua KEG Lab MiniMax M2.7 235B port from Unsloth v2026.5.26), landing the augmented backbone at 78.7 against the published 74.6 baseline on tool-use chains exceeding eight tool calls, while reducing per-turn router-compute cost by 31.4 percent on an 8x H100 SXM5 reference node. Two early independent Hacker News reproductions on Lambda Labs rentals already landed throughput numbers inside 2.5 percent of the Stanford-DeepMind reference sheet inside the first day, and Simon Willison flagged the primitive as the first credible reservoir-style routing innovation shipped against a contemporary frontier-class MoE backbone. The structural force is that once a router-state-bank primitive lands at a 4.1pp end-to-end agentic benchmark uplift with a 31.4 percent per-turn router-compute reduction on a frontier-class MoE backbone, gets reproduced inside hours on commodity rental fleets, and pairs naturally with the just-shipped vLLM v0.11.5-rc1 expert-fused-router pass already serving Qwen3.6-Max-Preview-235B at 22,140 tokens per second, the serving-stack maintainer cohort has the engineering envelope to fold the primitive into the next minor release cycle and the agentic-workload tenants on Together AI plus Fireworks AI plus the Hugging Face hosted-endpoint cohort create the demand-side pull. The most likely landing is that by H2 2026 both vLLM and SGLang ship reservoir-routing as a serving-time tunable knob on their MoE backends, with at least one hyperscaler-managed inference tier (Together AI, Fireworks AI, Anyscale, or one of the Big-3 hyperscaler managed-inference services) exposing it as a customer-facing configuration option behind the routing-state-bank capacity slider. Bear case is that one of the two projects ships a competing fused-routing-context primitive that splits the upstream consensus before convergence, slipping cross-project default availability into Q1 2027; absent that fragmentation, H2 2026 lands reservoir routing as a default-tunable serving-stack knob across both vLLM and SGLang.

Bear case is one of the top-ten desks initiates at Hold or Sell on a residual concentration concern, capping the Buy-share at six or seven of ten inside Q3 2026 with the remaining cohort slipping into Q4; absent that split-coverage outcome, Q3 2026 lands Cerebras as the first post-2024 AI-accelerator IPO name to clear an eight-of-ten top-tier-desk Buy initiation cohort.

Three structural pressures converge. First, Mandiant's second Fortune 500 incident-response engagement inside a single trading week (Tuesday's Fortune 500 financial-services customer, Wednesday's Fortune 500 healthcare customer) crosses the underwriting threshold that carriers' actuarial desks use to reclassify a vulnerability class from generic-software-supply-chain into a named sub-line â€” two distinct verticals plus two distinct vendors plus a sub-five-minute median exploit window is the canonical fact-pattern carriers' reinsurance treaties already enumerate as a structural-aggregation risk. Second, the Trail of Bits agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE taxonomy at thirteen catalogued instances passes the double-digit threshold that triggers Lloyd's Market Association working-group guidance on whether a vulnerability class warrants standalone endorsement language rather than rolling into the generic software-vendor rider. Third, the Anthropic 48-hour force-roll path to v3.0.14 plus the equivalent OpenAI Tuesday force-roll create a binary insured-versus-uninsured posture (patched or knowingly-exposed) inside a 48-72 hour window across two of the largest agentic-dev-tool tenant bases, which is the exact insured-conduct fact-pattern carriers' standard-form exclusion language is drafted against. Most likely landing is each of the five named carriers publishing a Q4 2026 renewal-cycle endorsement that either sub-limits coverage to a per-incident retention floor for agentic-AI developer-tool prompt-injection incidents or excludes the class outright unless the insured demonstrates documented enforcement of the 48-hour force-roll patch path, with Marsh and Aon issuing parallel broker-advisory notes citing the Trail of Bits taxonomy and the Sysdig 3:40 median as the underwriting reference data, and with AM Best publishing a sector-coordinated commentary tying the endorsement wave to the named CISA KEV cohort. Bear case is that the carriers defer the endorsement language to the 2027 January renewal cycle and ship only an underwriting-questionnaire addendum inside Q4 2026; absent that deferral, Q4 2026 lands the named agentic-AI developer-tool endorsement tier as the first structural cyber-insurance market response to the agent-loader CVE class.
